text: Harness decompose stage may ask one clarifying question instead of guessing children when the parent's intent is ambiguous
description: RESEARCHED: Deng et al., 'Uncertainty-Aware Clarification in LLM Agents with Information Gain', ICML 2026 (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/deng26l.html, arXiv 2606.03135) — scores candidate clarifying questions by the belief shift toward the user's true goal; Prism (arXiv 2601.08653) orders dependent questions to cut user load; ARIA Scaling Trust names 'security policy elicitation protocols … help user discover their goals' as fundable tooling (1754d0d8). OBSERVED: the decompose stage today must return children or a rationale for none; an ambiguous high-value parent gets guessed children. Proposal: add a third decompose outcome 'ask': the planner proposes up to 3 candidate questions, each with the 2-3 decompositions it would choose between depending on the answer; the harness picks the question whose answers lead to the most different child sets (cheap information-gain proxy: embedding distance between the alternative child sets), files it as an unclear child with the question and the alternatives in its status comment, and skips the parent until it is answered. Acceptance: stages.test for the 'ask' schema; cycle.test where an ask outcome creates one unclear child and no open children; on the decomposition eval set, report how often the planner asks. Refuted if, on parents Felix rated clear, the planner asks in more than ~20% of cases (noise), or if Felix's answers do not change the resulting children.

status.comment: Proposed by Claude from the 2026-11-09 research (goal elicitation papers + ARIA call). Accept to let the harness ask before decomposing; also strengthens the ARIA pitch (1754d0d8) if that is pursued.
